{{Quote|I'm the future! I'm the youngest of those born on high. All Sith after me are Kesh-born. The leader of the Sith should be special.|Jariad Korsin|<ref name="savior" />}}
'''Jariad Korsin''' was a [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[High Lord]] of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Kesh/Legends|Kesh's]] [[Lost Tribe of Sith]] in the [[Standard year/Legends|years]] following the [[Great Hyperspace War/Legends|Great Hyperspace War]]. The son of [[Sith mineralogical corps]] members [[Devore Korsin|Devore]] and [[Seelah Korsin]], Korsin was just an [[Youngling/Legends|infant]] on board the [[Sith dreadnaught]] ''[[Omen]]'' when it crashed on the remote, isolated world of Kesh after a [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Skirmish over Phaegon III|attack]] at the height of the Great Hyperspace War. Korsin survived the disaster along with his [[Parent/Legends|parents]], though soon after the crash Devore [[Duel near the Omen|died]] at the hands of his brother, ''Omen'' [[Captain/Legends|captain]] [[Yaru Korsin]], after an attempted power grab. The survivors soon took dominion over the planet's [[Keshiri/Legends|Keshiri]] natives and established the Lost Tribe of [[Sith/Legends|Sith]], with Yaru at its head. Although Korsin's mother [[Marriage/Legends|married]] Yaru in an effort to secure Korsin's future, she never lost a burning hatred of the former [[Sith invasion fleet|naval]] captain for Devore's [[Death/Legends|death]] and raised Korsin to share that fury.

Together, Korsin and his mother plotted for years to wreak their vengeance upon Yaru and install Korsin as the new [[Grand Lord]] of the Lost Tribe. In the meantime, Korsin became an extremely prominent figure in Keshiri society, using [[Politics/Legends|political]] flair and savvy to establish himself as a popular choice for future Grand [[Lord/Legends|Lordship]], and using his superior [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] [[Lightsaber combat/Legends|skills]] to lead the [[Sith Saber]] honor detail&mdash;which he secretly trained as a strike force in anticipation of his and Seelah's uprising. In [[4975 BBY]], they finally decided it was time to strike. [[Duel near the Kesh Sith Temple|Attacking]] the now-aged Yaru near the [[Takara Mountains|mountain]]-based [[Kesh Sith Temple]], Korsin and his Sith Sabers gained the upper hand and severely wounded the Grand Lord. However, the timely arrival of Korsin's half-sister [[Nida Korsin|Nida]] and her [[uvak]]-riding [[Skyborn Rangers]], fighting on Yaru's side, turned the tide of the battle, and Korsin eventually died in combat.

==Biography==
===Early life===
====Crash on Kesh====
{{Quote|We're already dead.|Seelah Korsin to Jariad and Yaru Korsin, after the ''Omen''{{'s}} crash on Kesh|<ref name="precipice" />}}
[[File:Omen_wreck.jpg|thumb|right|250px|The ''Omen'', after crashing on Kesh]]
A [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]],<ref name="savior" /> Jariad Korsin was [[Reproduction/Legends|born]]<ref name="precipice" /> around [[5000 BBY/Legends|5000 BBY]]<ref name="birth date" /> to [[Sith mineralogical corps]] members [[Devore Korsin|Devore]] and [[Seelah Korsin]]. That [[Standard year/Legends|year]], at the height of the [[Great Hyperspace War/Legends|Great Hyperspace War]] between the [[Sith Empire/Legends|Sith Empire]] and the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], the [[Youngling/Legends|infant]] Korsin accompanied<ref name="precipice" /> his<ref name="savior" /> [[Parent/Legends|parents]] on a [[Lignan crystal|Lignan]] [[Mining/Legends|mining]] mission to the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Phaegon III]]'s [[Phaegon III's largest moon|largest moon]]. Korsin and his family went aboard the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] [[Starship/Legends|starship]] ''[[Omen]]'', [[Captain/Legends|captained]] by Devore's half-brother, [[Yaru Korsin]]. However, the ''Omen'' came under [[Skirmish over Phaegon III|attack]] by [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]], causing it to veer off-course as the vessel jumped to [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]]. As the ship headed to parts unknown, a [[Gravity well/Legends|gravity well]] tore the ''Omen'' apart,<ref name="precipice" /> and the [[Sith dreadnaught]]<ref name="crosscurrent">''[[Crosscurrent]]''</ref> reverted back to [[Realspace/Legends|realspace]] toward a mysterious world known as [[Kesh/Legends|Kesh]].<ref name="precipice" /> 

Korsin survived the disaster in his mother's [[Limb/Legends|arms]], and as chaos erupted aboard the ''Omen'', Devore ordered his [[Marriage/Legends|wife]] to take Korsin with her to the [[Escape pod/Legends|escape pods]]. The escape pods were completely inaccessible, however, and instead, Seelah brought Korsin with her to the [[Bridge (starship)/Legends|bridge]], where the ever-volatile Devore was fighting with his brother over the ship's controls. After everyone took cover, the ''Omen'' hurtled into Kesh's [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmosphere]], eventually smashing into a [[Takara Mountains|mountain range]]. Although the ship was destroyed, the infant Korsin, along with his family, survived the crash.<ref name="precipice" /> 

Among 355 survivors, the Korsins made their way to a clearing below the crash site, a treacherous journey in which twenty-one [[Death/Legends|perished]]. Those who remained set up a rudimentary camp, where Korsin spent more [[Time/Legends|time]] with Devore while his mother focused on [[Medic/Legends|treating]] the injured and sick. Not long after the crash, Devore made an ill-fated attempt to wrest control of the group from Yaru, leading to a [[Duel near the Omen|lightsaber duel]] and Devore's death. Korsin and his mother were kept unaware about the circumstances of Devore's demise, which had occurred away from the camp near the remains of the ''Omen''.<ref name="precipice" /> 

====Growing up Sith====
{{Quote|You've changed the world today.''"<br />"''He's not who I want to kill.|Seelah and Jariad Korsin, after the slaying of Ravilan Wroth|<ref name="paragon" />}}
Through the chance arrival of an indigenous [[Keshiri/Legends|Keshiri]] woman, [[Adari Vaal]], the Sith were able to escape their entrapment in the [[Mountain/Legends|mountains]], posing as the native [[Skyborn|gods]] to gain the allegiance of the Keshiri masses. The Sith were moved into the homes of the Keshiri ruling council, the [[Neshtovar]], and Korsin lived with his mother and Yaru in Neshtovar leader [[Izri Dazh]]'s house. Although the Sith were eager to find a way off the remote planet, they soon found there was none, and Korsin grew up in isolation from the rest of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]].<ref name="skyborn">''[[Lost Tribe of the Sith: Skyborn]]''</ref>

[[File:Tahv.jpg|thumb|left|250px|The city Tahv, where Korsin spent some of his childhood.]]
In the coming years, the survivors of the ''Omen'' crash formed a new Sith organization known as the [[Lost Tribe of Sith]], with Yaru firmly at its head as [[Grand Lord]]. Korsin's mother married Yaru and bore him a daughter, [[Nida Korsin|Nida]], in an attempt to secure the future of herself and her son. As a result, Korsin was brought up in relative luxury, first in the [[Capital/Legends|capital]] [[City/Legends|city]] of [[Tahv]] and later in the [[Kesh Sith Temple]] high in the mountains near the ''Omen''{{'s}} wreckage. At some point, Seelah came to believe that Yaru had been responsible for Devore's death and instilled in Korsin a burning hatred for his stepfather. Together, they plotted to get their revenge on the Grand [[Lord/Legends|Lord]] and place Korsin at the helm of the Lost Tribe. One of their first objectives was to remove the [[Sith (species)/Legends|pureblood Sith]] element from the Lost Tribe, in an effort to instill an [[Humanocentrism|all-Human purity]] in the group.<ref name="paragon" /> 

In [[4985 BBY]], Korsin's mother was at the forefront of a conspiracy to frame the few [[Blood/Legends|purebloods]] who still remained in the Tribe for several massacres of Keshiri in the southern towns of the [[Ragnos Lakes]] region, actually engineered by Seelah herself. The misdirection was a complete success: Yaru became convinced of the purebloods' complicity in the deaths and ordered a wholesale [[Red Sith Purge|purge]] of the beings from the face of Kesh. The [[Speciecide|genocide]] lasted a single night, toward the end of which the pureblood leader, [[Ravilan Wroth]], was captured and held in a public plaza in Tahv. After a short, tense conversation between Seelah and Wroth, Korsin leaped from the shadows, wielding a [[Vibroblade/Legends|vibroblade]]. He then drew his [[Sith lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] and killed Wroth. Seelah commended him, but Jariad complained that he actually wished to kill Yaru, to which his mother urged patience.<ref name="paragon" />

===Adult life===
====Plan in motion====
{{Quote|Grand Lord, I request permission to remove the Sabers to the Northern Reaches for a training mission. There, they can concentrate.''"<br />"''Hmm? Oh, certainly.|Jariad Korsin and Yaru Korsin|<ref name="savior" />}}
[[File:Yaru_Korsin.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Yaru Korsin, Jariad Korsin's uncle and later stepfather]]
As Korsin grew into a man, he gained a reputation as something of a wild child, which he would shed as he came of age and became a popular choice to succeed Yaru as Grand Lord. Around [[4975 BBY]], now&ndash;[[High Lord]] Korsin founded the [[Sith Saber]]s, a ceremonial honor detail that specialized in [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] feats, placing himself as head with Yaru's blessing. That year, with all endeavors to find a way off Kesh foiled, the Lost Tribe of Sith decided to commit to staying on Kesh for good. Their intentions were announced in a massive celebration in Tahv's [[Circle Eternal]] plaza. The ceremony featured a demonstration by the Sith Sabers, led by Korsin. By then, Korsin's mother had grown absolutely certain that Yaru was responsible for Devore's death twenty-five years prior, and as the celebration drew to a close, Seelah assured Korsin that their time for vengeance was at hand.<ref name="savior" />

Over the past several [[Standard week/Legends|weeks]], Korsin had ramped up heavier combat training for his Sabers, whom he meant to serve as his strike force. After the ceremony, Korsin enacted the first part of their plan&mdash;misdirection. Korsin staged a practice [[Lightsaber duel/Legends|duel]] with his Sith Sabers in front of Yaru, soundly thrashing them, and even [[Cho mai/Legends|severing]] one of his Sabers' hands. He then proclaimed that he was taking them to the distant [[Northern Reaches]] for training, hoping to ensure that Yaru, even if he did suspect that Korsin and Seelah were up to something, would not expect them to strike anytime soon. The phase went off without a hitch, as Korsin received his stepfather's permission to remove his Sabers to the Northern Reaches.<ref name="savior" />

====Duel and death====
{{Quote|It's time to make your reckoning, ''Commander'' Korsin. You told us yourself. A new age has dawned. It's time for military authority to end. This is about succession&mdash;who should best lead the Tribe.|Jariad Korsin, to Yaru Korsin|<ref name="savior" />}}
[[File:KeshSithTemple.jpg|thumb|left|250px|The Kesh Sith Temple, the site of Jariad Korsin's death]]
Later on, while Yaru paced the Kesh [[Sith temple/Legends|Sith Temple]] accompanied by his [[Houk/Legends|Houk]] friend [[Gloyd]] and four [[Bodyguard/Legends|bodyguards]], Korsin gathered his Sabers and ambushed his target. Before Yaru could react, Korsin had him surrounded, outnumbered four-to-one. Seelah soon appeared and joined the standoff, but as the two sides faced each other down, suddenly dozens of [[uvak]] beasts rose to the sky. As it happened, a secret [[Keshiri resistance]] group headed by Adari Vaal had chosen that moment to carry out their final plan, which involved the theft of the uvak beasts vital to Sith dominion over Kesh. The rise of the uvak provided just enough of a diversion to allow Yaru to break the circle and flee to better ground. A full-scale [[Duel near the Kesh Sith Temple|lightsaber duel]] was on. Although Yaru battled back valiantly, his force was dwindling, and he began to lose strength.<ref name="savior" />

Korsin finally cornered the Grand Lord near a high precipice and released all his anger, furiously slashing at him again and again. However, as Korsin moved in for the kill, his sister Nida suddenly appeared on uvak-back with members of her [[Skyborn Rangers]] riding club. Nida and her Rangers were the last trick up Yaru's sleeve, and they flew into the fray and turned the tide of the battle. Korsin fought his sister in a desperate attempt to repel their advance, but he himself was wounded. In his last moments, Yaru attempted to throw Korsin over the precipice&mdash;although the Grand Lord failed, Nida did it instead, and Korsin fell to his death. With Korsin's slaying, Seelah's plots were completely foiled. Yaru soon died from his injuries, and Nida Korsin took over the mantle of Grand Lord.<ref name="savior" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|Captain, I wouldn't put this one in charge of mucking out the uvak stalls.|Gloyd, commenting on Jariad Korsin's unsuitability to succeed his father as Grand Lord|<ref name="savior" />}}
Influenced by his mother from a young age, Jariad Korsin always harbored a burning, homicidal hatred of his stepfather, Yaru Korsin. Korsin was very loyal to his mother, killing at her command as early as his teens.<ref name="paragon" /> Although once a wild child, Korsin matured somewhat as he entered his twenties and gained a certain [[Politics/Legends|political]] savvy&mdash;he carried himself in public with a resolute swagger, making every pause a pose for history. Although he never knew his biological father, Devore, Korsin took after him greatly. Self-absorbed, Korsin was apt to cut corners just as his father was, either doing nothing or overdoing it. Korsin saw himself as the future of the Lost Tribe and was quick to proclaim that destiny to his stepfather as he faced him down near the Kesh Sith Temple before their fateful battle. Ultimately, it was these traits inherited from his father that doomed Korsin to his demise, as he was thrown to his death from the same precipice where Devore had met his end. Nearly a third of a [[Meter/Legends|meter]] taller than his stepfather Yaru, Korsin had [[Color/Legends|tan]] skin, jet-black long [[Hair/Legends|hair]], and a black beard.<ref name="savior" />

==Powers and abilities==
{{Quote|They were too quickly disarmed.|Jariad Korsin, after easily defeating several lightsaber-wielding foes|<ref name="savior" />}}
[[File:Uvak.jpg|thumb|right|250px|An uvak creature, which Korsin could ride]]
Both of Jariad Korsin's parents were [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]],<ref name="paragon" /> and Korsin inherited that quality from them at birth.<ref name="savior" /> Growing up in the Lost Tribe, Korsin was trained in the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]], and by his teen years he had become adept with both a lightsaber and a vibroblade.<ref name="paragon" /> By the time he reached his twenties and had become the head of the Sith Sabers, Korsin's skill with a lightsaber had improved greatly; he was able to dispatch multiple armed attackers without exerting much energy. However, his saber skills, as excellent as they were, were not sufficient to prevent his death in 4975 BBY. In that fateful battle, Korsin's incompetence as a trainer reared its head, as his Sabers found themselves unprepared for the fight. Korsin was a capable uvak-rider, as the winged beasts provided the primary mode of transportation for the Lost Tribe in his time.<ref name="savior" />

==Equipment==
{{Quote|Are you sure you want to call this group of yours the Sabers? They seem to be without.|Yaru Korsin to Jariad Korsin, after the latter disarmed all of his Sith Sabers using his own lightsaber|<ref name="savior" />}}
Korsin wielded a vibroblade and a red lightsaber during his teenage years,<ref name="paragon" /> and continued utilizing his lightsaber into his adulthood. As a Sith Saber, Korsin wore their black uniform.<ref name="savior" />

==Behind the scenes==
Jariad Korsin first appeared in [[John Jackson Miller]]'s [[2009]] [[eBook]], ''[[Lost Tribe of the Sith: Precipice]]'', the first installment in the [[Star Wars: Lost Tribe of the Sith|''Lost Tribe of the Sith'']] series.<ref name="precipice" />
